cleanIntro: The TP9 SFx is a competition-length striker pistol and its field strip is the standard Canik sequence: unload, press the trigger to lower the striker, pull the two takedown catches above the trigger down, and push the slide forward off the frame. The red striker indicator disappearing is your confirmation the striker is down. Two things to check before you start: if your barrel is threaded, the muzzle protector must come off BEFORE disassembly, and the whole Suppressor Ready Models chapter at the back is scoped to suppressed models only. Note also a publisher slip in this book — the warranty page names the TTI COMBAT, boilerplate carried over from a different model's manual.

steps.title: Magazine out, slide back, chamber inspected
steps.action: Keep the pistol pointed somewhere safe, press the magazine release with your thumb and let the magazine drop into your free hand. Then grasp the slide under the rear sight, run it fully rearward and hold it open while you look into the chamber. Let it forward on the empty chamber and press the trigger to lower the striker — when the striker is down the red indicator at the back of the slide is not visible.
steps.prose: That red indicator is the only external tell on this pistol. Learn to look for its absence.
steps.quote: 1. While keeping the pistol pointed in a safe direction, hold the pistol with one hand, depress the magazine release button with your thumb and the magazine should fall into your free hand. (See lllustration #6) 2. Grasp the slide under the rear sight and move it fully rearward, holding the slide fully open inspect the chamber to ensure it is empty.

steps.title: Threaded barrel? The protector comes off first
steps.action: If your SFx has a threaded muzzle, unscrew the thread protector before you go any further — Canik states it must be off before disassembly. The wrench is in the case, and the direction depends on your barrel: on a metric left-hand barrel you unscrew CLOCKWISE, which is the opposite of what your hand expects. If your barrel is not threaded this whole section does not apply to you.
steps.prose: Thread pitch varies between metric and inch configurations on this model, so check the barrel rather than assuming.
steps.caution: WARNING! Threaded muzzle protector must be taken off before disassembly.
steps.quote: Notice! This section only applies to threaded barrel configurations.

steps.title: Secure the pistol, then lower the striker
steps.action: Rest the unloaded pistol firmly on your lap or a table with the muzzle in a safe direction and press the trigger to lower the striker. This is a required part of the sequence: the takedown catches will not free the slide with the striker cocked. Confirm the red striker indicator has disappeared before you touch the catches.
steps.prose: Doing this with the gun held out in mid-air is how people end up fighting the catches one-handed.
steps.quote: 1. While remembering to maintain a safe muzzle direction, secure the unloaded pistol firmly in a supported location such as your lap, or on a table. Pull the trigger to lower the striker.

steps.warn: Muzzle in a safe direction before the trigger is touched.

steps.title: Both takedown catches down, slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Hold the pistol in your primary hand and pull BOTH takedown catches — the pair sitting just above the trigger — straight down using the index finger and thumb of your other hand. With them held down, push the slide forward with the thumb of your primary hand until it runs off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: Both catches, together. One alone leaves the other side engaged and it feels exactly like a seized slide.
steps.caution: Wear eye protection — the recoil spring is next.
steps.quote: 2. While holding the pistol in your primary hand, grasp the take down catches, located above the trigger. Pull them down using index finger and thumb of your secondary hand (See lllustration #7). When the takedown catch is pulled down, the slide will move  forward slightly. After that, by use the thumb of your primary hand to push the slide forward until it is free from the frame. (lllustration #8)

steps.title: Recoil spring out, barrel out
steps.action: Hold the slide upside down. Push the recoil spring toward the muzzle against its own tension to unseat it, then lift it free. With the spring out, lift the barrel slightly, push it forward toward the muzzle, then draw it back and up out of the slide. That is the whole strip.
steps.prose: The spring is captive but it is still loaded until it clears. Keep a thumb over it.
steps.aside: 2. Lift the barrel slightly and push it forward toward the muzzle. Then you can pull it back and lift it free from the slide.
steps.quote: 1. Holding the slide with primary hand, use your secondary hand to push the recoil spring toward the muzzle and lift it free. (See lllustration #9)

steps.title: Bore from the chamber to the muzzle
steps.action: Attach the correct calibre nylon bore brush to the rod, dampen it with CLP and push and pull it through the barrel several times from the CHAMBER to the MUZZLE. Then swap to a cloth patch on the rod and push it through several times to carry the loosened fouling out. Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then leave a light coating of CLP in the bore.
steps.prose: Chamber-to-muzzle keeps the brush off the crown and moves fouling the way the bullet went.
steps.aside: Repeat this process with the brush and cleaning patches until a final patch comes out clean after swabbing the bore.
steps.quote: 4. Dampen the screw-in nylon bore brush with cleaner, lubricant, protectant (CLP) and then push/pull the brush through the barrel several times from the chamber to the muzzle.

steps.title: Where the CLP actually goes
steps.action: Take the shooting residue off the slide, the barrel exterior and the action parts with the brush and cloth, then put a light coat of CLP on a specific short list: the frame rails, the trigger bar, the inside of the ejector assembly, the rails on the slide, the firing pin block, and the slide's inner surface where the barrel rides. Everywhere else gets wiped, not oiled.
steps.prose: That list is Canik's, and it is short on purpose. A striker gun with oil everywhere collects grit in the frame.
steps.quote: 7. Remove shooting residue from the slide, barrel's exterior, and action parts using the brush and cloth supplied. Apply a light coating of CLP to the rails, trigger bar and inside of the ejector assembly of frame and rails on the slide and firing pin block together with the slide's inner side where the barrel operates.

steps.title: Nothing abrasive, ever
steps.action: Do not take sandpaper or emery cloth to any part of this pistol. Canik's reasoning is mechanical rather than cosmetic: anything more aggressive than a Scotch Brite damages the precision contact surfaces, and a damaged contact surface creates friction, and friction on a striker pistol is a malfunction. Solvents go in a well-ventilated area away from open flames.
steps.prose: This bites people trying to polish a feed ramp or scrub a stubborn carbon ring off the breech face.
steps.quote: WARNING! MAINTAINING THE FINISH ON YOUR PISTOL Do not use sandpaper or emery cloth to clean any part of the firearm or suppressor. Abrasives more aggressive than Scotch Brite may damage the precision contact surfaces of the pistol, resulting in friction that can lead to malfunctions of the firearm and suppressor.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring — four parts and no tools. The disassembly chapter of this book ends there and nothing deeper is published for the SFx. Reassembly is the reverse, with the flat end of the recoil spring facing the chamber.
steps.prose: Anything beyond this is not published by Canik for this pistol.

deepAbsentReason: Canik publishes NO deeper procedure for this pistol. The book's Disassembly chapter consists of exactly two steps — recoil spring out and barrel out — and stops. Every other teardown in the manual is an accessory or configuration job scoped by the manual itself: the thread protector ('this section only applies to threaded barrel configurations'), the optic sight interface and its lid, the magazine release button extensions, the backstrap, and the Suppressor Ready Models chapter ('this section is for suppressed models only'). None of them is a deeper clean of the pistol, so there is nothing published to walk. Canik also warns that any part installed other than a CANiK Accessory Program part voids the warranty and may damage the pistol, and that failure to follow the disassembly and assembly instructions may damage it — inventing a striker or fire-control teardown here would be substitution.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Correct calibre nylon bore brush on the rod, dampened with CLP
Push/pull through the barrel several times from the CHAMBER to the MUZZLE
Cloth patches on the rod until a final patch comes out clean
Light coating of CLP left in the bore

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Brush and cloth to take shooting residue off the slide and the barrel exterior
Light CLP on the slide rails, the firing pin block, and the inner surface where the barrel operates
Nothing abrasive — no sandpaper, no emery cloth

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Residue off the action parts with the supplied brush and cloth
Light CLP on the frame rails, the trigger bar and inside the ejector assembly
Wipe the outer surfaces with a soft cloth dipped in good quality gun oil

cleaning.name: THREADED / SUPPRESSED MODELS ONLY
tasks: The muzzle protector must come off before disassembly
Thread pattern is M13,5 LH or 1/2-28 RH — fitting anything else destroys pistol and suppressor
Never fire lead, frangible or pre-fragmented ammunition with a suppressor installed
Standard pressure only through a suppressor — not +P

reassembly: Hold the slide muzzle-down, drop the barrel in, then turn the slide muzzle-up and let the barrel settle into place.
Put the recoil spring into the muzzle end of the slide with its FLAT end facing the chamber, and press it toward the muzzle and slightly down with your thumb.
Align the slide cutouts with the frame rails and pull the slide fully rearward.
Rack the slide to confirm it has assembled correctly before anything else.
If the barrel is threaded, refit the thread protector — metric left-hand barrels tighten ANTICLOCKWISE.
fncheck: With the pistol empty, rack the slide fully and let it go forward under its own spring rather than riding it, and confirm it returns to battery every time. Check the takedown catches have risen back into place — a slide that is on but not latched will come off under recoil. Press the trigger and confirm it breaks and then resets when the slide is cycled, and check the red striker indicator appears when the striker is cocked and disappears when it is down. Finally seat an empty magazine and confirm the slide locks back.
